_readme: Single source of truth for the vocabulary that crosses the backend/ml boundary.
backend/ (TypeScript) is the canonical live scorer: src/config/detection.ts owns LLR_TABLE,
MonitoringChannel is defined in backend/prisma/schema.prisma.
ml/ (Python) is the offline calibration + evaluation lab: src/vtml/detectors/schema.py owns
REGISTRY, Channel is defined in src/vtml/types.py.
Neither file imports the other today. This file exists so the two vocabularies are recorded
side by side instead of drifting silently -- see docs/cross-component-architecture.md.
HOW TO KEEP THIS IN SYNC:
1. backend/prisma/schema.prisma's `enum MonitoringChannel` is authoritative for
monitoringChannels.values -- if you change the enum, update this file in the same change.
2. ml/src/vtml/detectors/schema.py's REGISTRY is authoritative for mlDetectorTypes -- if you
add/remove/rename a DetectorType or its wire_channel, update this file in the same change.
3. backend/src/config/detection.ts's LLR_TABLE is authoritative for backendDetectorTypes --
same rule.
4. backend/tests/unit/detection-contract.test.ts and ml/tests/test_contract.py both load this
file and fail if their local source drifts from it. Run both before merging a change here.
5. `typeMapping` is no longer documentation only: backend/src/config/calibrated-weights.ts
reads it to adopt ml's fitted calibration curves as LLR_TABLE magnitudes. Changing an entry
changes which backend detector type a fitted curve lands on, so change it with the same care
as a constant. backend/tests/unit/calibrated-weights.test.ts asserts every adopted override
went through this map. A CV/ASR producer emitting ml-shaped types at the internal API is
still an unbuilt use for the same mapping.

channelMapping._readme: ml's 6 channels are coarser than backend's 11. This is the mapping ml/src/vtml/wire.py already implements at the observation level (via wire_channel per detector type, not a flat channel-to-channel map) -- recorded here at channel granularity for quick reference.

channelMappingNotes.network: No MonitoringChannel value exists for it. ml/wire.py turns a network observation into an UnscoredWindow (reason SIGNAL_LOSS) instead -- a dropped connection is never scored, on either side (backend Architecture.md §6.6 agrees independently).
channelMappingNotes.audio: Declared on both sides but inert in v1. ml/wire.py never puts it on the wire. Backend's `second_voice` LLR_TABLE entry exists but is not emitted by any backend detector -- reserved for a future ASR producer.
channelMappingNotes.POINTER: Backend MonitoringChannel value with no ml equivalent -- PRD names no pointer/mouse-movement detector in ml v1 (ml/docs/Memory.md, 2026-09-18 decision).
channelMappingNotes.IDENTITY, SCREEN, ENVIRONMENT: Backend MonitoringChannel values with no ml equivalent at all -- backend-only concepts (device/environment change detectors, identity checks) that ml's 6-channel model never modeled.

backendDetectorTypes._readmeEmitted: emittedByClientDetector: types actually produced by backend/src/live/detectors/*.ts today.
backendDetectorTypes._readmeReserved: reservedForExternalProducer: types with an LLR_TABLE entry but no client detector -- only reachable today via POST /api/v1/internal/:id/observations (CV/ASR producers, backend Architecture.md §2). No producer sends these yet.

reservedForExternalProducer.visibility_loss: intended for a screen/camera-visibility CV signal
reservedForExternalProducer.face_absent: intended for a face-detection CV signal
reservedForExternalProducer.multiple_faces: intended for a face-count CV signal
reservedForExternalProducer.gaze_away: intended for a gaze-tracking CV signal
reservedForExternalProducer.foreign_object: a phone, book, second laptop or similar object visible on camera (browser-side object detector)
reservedForExternalProducer.second_voice: intended for a second-speaker ASR signal

backendDetectorTypes.openQuestion: visibility_loss and face_absent carry near-identical LLR values (0.8/1.2/1.8 vs 0.9/1.4/2.0) and no detector distinguishes their intended trigger. Worth resolving with whoever wires the first CV producer, not decided here.

_readmeTypeMapping: typeMapping: ml detector type -> the backend detector type it is conceptually equivalent to. NOW WIRED: backend/src/config/calibrated-weights.ts reads this map at startup to adopt ml's fitted curves as LLR_TABLE magnitudes, behind the CALIBRATED_WEIGHTS_ENABLED flag (off by default). Backend types are coarser (12 vs ml's 16) and several ml types collapse into one backend type, so a backend type is adopted only when exactly one *fitted* ml type maps to it -- there is no defensible way to merge two curves into one value. See docs/cross-component-architecture.md.

typeMappingNotes.network.*: No backend equivalent -- backend never scores network/signal-loss as evidence (see channelMappingNotes.network). These three ml types would all become an UnscoredWindow, never an LLR_TABLE lookup.
typeMappingNotes.unmapped_backend_types_note: No ml equivalent -- ml's 6-channel model has no device/screen-count concept.
